tier1.text: The pelvic girdle attaches a lower limb to the axial skeleton, the bones of the head and trunk. The pelvic girdle, also called the hip girdle, is formed by a single bone, the hip bone. Built to steady and support the body, the pelvic girdle moves very little. Most muscles that attach to and move the femur, or thigh bone, start on the pelvic girdle.

quotes.quote: The pelvic girdle (hip girdle) is formed by a single bone, the hip bone or coxal bone (coxal = “hip”), which serves as the attachment point for each lower limb.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: There is very little movement of the pelvic girdle because of its connection with the sacrum at the base of the axial skeleton. The pelvic girdle has less range of motion because it was designed to stabilize and support the body.
